### Setting up Populations

Below are some parameters for setting up the populations.

```{r}
set.seed(123)
n_indv <- 45
n_loci <- 15
n_pop <- 3

```

### Defining Reference Populations

There will be five generated populations each with unique allele frequencies defined by me.

```{r}
#Population 1
p_1 <- 0.6
q_1 <- 1 - p_1
Pop_1 <- data.frame(matrix(sample(c("AA", "Aa", "aa"), size = n_indv * n_loci, replace = TRUE,prob = c(p_1^2, 2 * p_1 * q_1, q_1^2)),nrow = n_indv,ncol = n_loci))
rownames(Pop_1) <- paste0("Indv_A.", 1:n_indv)
colnames(Pop_1) <- paste0("Genotype_Locus", 1:n_loci)


#Population 2
p_2 <- 0.2
q_2 <- 1 - p_2

Pop_2 <- data.frame(matrix(sample(c("AA", "Aa", "aa"), size = n_indv * n_loci, replace = TRUE,prob = c(p_2^2, 2 * p_2 * q_2, q_2^2)),nrow = n_indv,ncol = n_loci))
rownames(Pop_2) <- paste0("Indv_B.", 1:n_indv)
colnames(Pop_2) <- paste0("Genotype_Locus", 1:n_loci)

#Population 3
p_3 <- 0.9
q_3 <- 1 - p_3
Pop_3 <- data.frame(matrix(sample(c("AA", "Aa", "aa"), size = n_indv * n_loci, replace = TRUE,prob = c(p_3^2, 2 * p_3 * q_3, q_3^2)),nrow = n_indv,ncol = n_loci))
rownames(Pop_3) <- paste0("Indv_C.", 1:n_indv)
colnames(Pop_3) <- paste0("Genotype_Locus", 1:n_loci)

#Population 4
p_4 <- 0.5
q_4 <- 1 - p_4
Pop_4 <- data.frame(matrix(sample(c("AA", "Aa", "aa"), size = n_indv * n_loci, replace = TRUE,prob = c(p_4^2, 2 * p_4 * q_4, q_4^2)),nrow = n_indv,ncol = n_loci))
rownames(Pop_4) <- paste0("Indv_D.", 1:n_indv)
colnames(Pop_4) <- paste0("Genotype_Locus", 1:n_loci)

#Population 5
p_5 <- 0.7
q_5 <- 1 - p_5
Pop_5 <- data.frame(matrix(sample(c("AA", "Aa", "aa"), size = n_indv * n_loci, replace = TRUE,prob = c(p_5^2, 2 * p_5 * q_5, q_5^2)),nrow = n_indv,ncol = n_loci))
rownames(Pop_5) <- paste0("Indv_E", 1:n_indv)
colnames(Pop_5) <- paste0("Genotype_Locus", 1:n_loci)

head(Pop_1)
head(Pop_2)
head(Pop_3)
head(Pop_4)
head(Pop_5)
```

### Defining Deviated Populations

These are generated populations each with unique allele frequencies defined by me to simulate deviations from HWE, such as habitat fragmentation, genetic migration and inbreeding.

```{r}


#Population 6: Mirrors Population 1 but shows consequences of inbreeding after x generations

#The inbreeding co-efficient  (F) is "The probability that an individual has two alleles at a locus that are identical by descent, ranging from 0 (non-inbred) to 1 (completely inbred). Since it reflects the degree of inbreeding in a population, it influences the frequency and homozygotes and heterozygotes."
#FIS: INBREEDING WITHIN A SINGLE SUB-POPULAITON

# Pedigree F = (sum) (1/2 ^ (n + n' + 1 )) * 1 + Fa
#Fa is the inbreeding coefficient of an ancestor and n and n' are the number of generations from each parent to the common ancestor.

#F(ROH) is the genomic F; which is obtained by assessing runs of homozygosity. Actual autozygosty can vary to a wider degree than the pedigree expected average. 
#Offspring of self-fertilization F = 0.50. An example species could be Agave americana :3
#Offspring of full-siblings or parent-offspring F = 0.25
#Offspring of half-siblings F = 0.125(1-F)
#Offspring of first cousings F = 0.0625 


#Introducing the F-value within the genotype (?) frequency equation looks like: 
#Since inbreeding redistributes genotypes, allele frequencies themselves do not change. 
#Homo A' = p^2 + pF (or, p^2 + pqF)
#homo A = q^2 + pqF
#heterozygote: 2pq(1-F)
F_valuesP6 <- c(0.0625, 0.125, 0.25, 0.5)
F_p6 <- sample(F_valuesP6, 1)
F_p6
F_p6 <- 0.5
p_1 <- 0.6 
q_1 <- 1 - p_6 
Pop_6 <- data.frame(matrix(sample(c("AA", "Aa", "aa"), size = n_indv * n_loci, replace = TRUE,prob = c(p_1^2, ((2 * p_1 * q_1) * (1 - F_p6)), q_1^2)),nrow = n_indv, ncol = n_loci)) 
rownames(Pop_6) <- paste0("Indv_F.", 1:n_indv) 
colnames(Pop_6) <- paste0("Genotype_Locus", 1:n_loci)
Pop_6

#Sampled loci to compare are:1, 7, & 11




#Population 7: Mirrors Population 2 but shows consequences of genetic drift after x generations
#MODULE 4 CONCEPTS!!!!!!  
#FST: INBREEDING BETWEEN SUBPOPULATIONS
#FIT: INBREEDING ACROSS THE WHOLE POPULATION

#Heterozygous affect 2(pq)(1-Fst)
#pq in above equations have little hats, basically the same as population 6's equation but fashionable
#values of 0.00-0.05 show little to no drift. There is high gene flow
#values of 0.05-0.15 show moderate, ongoing genetic drift in partially isolated subpopulations with limited gene flow
#values of 0.15-0.25 shows strong genetic drift and polonged isolation; sub-populations have noticably diverged in allele frequencies
#values greater then 0.25 show severe-drift or near coplete isolation. Subpopulations are approachinng fixation for different alleles (FST = 1.0 for complete fixation)

F_values_P7 <- c(0.05, 0.10, 0.15, 0.20, 0.25)
Fst_p7 <- sample(F_values, 1)
Fst_p7
#calculate p hat and q hat...
p_2 <- 0.2
q_2 <- 1 - p_2
Pop_7 <- data.frame(matrix(sample(c("AA", "Aa", "aa"), size = n_indv * n_loci, replace = TRUE,prob = c(p_2^2, ((2 * p_2 * q_2) * (1 - F)), q_2^2)),nrow = n_indv,ncol = n_loci)) 
rownames(Pop_7) <- paste0("Indv_G.", 1:n_indv) 
colnames(Pop_7) <- paste0("Genotype_Locus", 1:n_loci)  
Pop_7

#Population 8: Mirrors Population 3 but shows consequences of fixation 
F_values_P8 <- c(0.25, 0.35, 0.45, 0.55, 0.65, 0.75, 0.85, 0.95)
Fst_p8 <- sample(F_values_P8, 1)
Fst_p8
#need to calculate pq hat from pop3
p_3 <- 0.9
q_3 <- 1 - p_3
Pop_8 <- data.frame(matrix(sample(c("AA", "Aa", "aa"), size = n_indv * n_loci, replace = TRUE,prob = c(p_3^2, 2 * p_3 * q_3, q_3^2)),nrow = n_indv,ncol = n_loci)) 
rownames(Pop_8) <- paste0("Indv_H.", 1:n_indv) 
colnames(Pop_8) <- paste0("Genotype_Locus", 1:n_loci)   

#could also show founder effect, maybe. genetic migration may be  abit more difficult, requiring a random sampling of allele frequencies from a parental thingy with its own sampling thingies

#Negative Assortive mating results in a negative Fis value which increases heterozygosity 
#Genetic drift or inbreednig effect of small populations shows that all individuals of a small population eventually become related over time, which increases the population's average Fst, leading to a gradual loss of heterozygosity. 
```

### Genotype Counts and Frequencies

Genotype counts are bound per population at the sampled locus. The same formula is used for defining and binding each population's genotype frequencies.

```{r}
#Binding genotype counts per (original) population

#Testing locus 5 at populations 1, 2, 3 

gc_locus3 <- rbind(table(Pop_1$Genotype_Locus3), table(Pop_2$Genotype_Locus3), table(Pop_3$Genotype_Locus3))
rownames(gc_locus3) <- c("Pop_1", "Pop_2", "Pop_3")

#Checking table

gc_locus3
```

```{r}

#Defining frequencies for Locus 5

fq_locus3 <- gc_locus3 / sum(gc_locus3)
fq_locus3 <- round(fq_locus3, digits = 3)
rownames(fq_locus3) <- c("Pop_1", "Pop_2", "Pop_3")

fq_locus3


```

### Calculating Heterozygosity and Homozygosity

```{r}
#Homozygosity & Heterozygosity percentages

#Locus 3
HMP1L3 <- sum(gc_locus3[1,1] + gc_locus3[1,3]) / sum(gc_locus3[2,]) * 100
HTP1L3 <- 100 - HMP1L3
HMP1L3
HTP1L3
Pop1_HTHM <- cbind(HTP1L3, HMP1L3)
Pop1_HTHM

HMP2L3 <- sum(gc_locus3[2,1] + gc_locus3[2,3]) / sum(gc_locus3[3,]) * 100
HTP2L3 <- 100 - HMP2L3
HMP2L3
HTP2L3

HMP3L3<- sum(gc_locus3[3,1] + gc_locus3[3,3]) / sum(gc_locus3[3,]) * 100
HTP3L3 <- 100 - HMP3L3
HTP3L3
HMP3L3


P_HTL3 <- c(HTP1L3, HTP2L3, HTP3L3)
P_HTL3 <- round(P_HTL3, digits = 3)


P_HML3 <- c(HMP1L3, HMP2L3, HMP3L3)
P_HML3 <- round(P_HML3, digits = 3)

P_HTL3
P_HML3


RBHHL3 <- rbind(P_HML3, P_HTL3)
RBHHL3.1 <- cbind(P_HTL3, P_HML3)


colnames(RBHHL3) <- c("Pop_1", "Pop_2", "Pop_3")
rownames(RBHHL3) <- c("Homozygosity % ", "Heterozygosity %")
RBHHL3
RBHHL3.1
```

### Expected and Observed allele freq

```{r}
#Observed allele frequencies at each sampled population: L11

O_P2L3 <- c(p2o =  2 * (fq_locus3[1,2] + fq_locus3[1,3]) / (2 * n_indv))

O_P2L3
O_Q2L3 <-c( 1 - O_P2L3 )

O_Q2L3

O_P3L3 <- c(p3o =  2 * (fq_locus3[2,2] + fq_locus3[2,3]) / (2 * n_indv))
O_P3L3 <- round(O_P3L3, digits = 3)
O_P3L3

O_Q3L3

O_P4L3 <- c(p2o =  2 * (fq_locus3[3,2] + fq_locus3[3,3]) / (2 * n_indv))
O_P4L3 <- round(O_P4L3, digits = 3)
O_P4L3
O_Q4L3 <-c( 1 - O_P4L3 )
O_Q4L3 <- round(O_Q4L3, digits = 3)
O_Q4L3

AOPFL3 <- cbind(O_P2L3, O_P3L3, O_P4L3)
AOQFL3 <- cbind(O_Q2L3, O_Q3L3, O_Q4L3)

AOAFL3 <- rbind(AOPFL3, AOQFL3)

AOAFL3

E_P2L3

E_Q2L3 <- round(E_Q2L3, digits = 3)
E_Q2L3

E_P3L3 <- c(p =  (2 * p_3 * q_3) / (2 * n_indv))
E_P3L3 <- round(E_P3L3, digits = 3)
E_P3L3
E_Q3L3 <- c( 1 - E_P3L3)
E_Q3L3 <- round(E_Q3L3, digits = 3)
E_Q3L3

E_P4L3 <- c(p =  (2 * p_4 * q_4) / (2 * n_indv))
E_P4L3 <- round(E_P4L3, digits = 3)
E_P4L3
E_Q4L3 <- c( 1 - E_P4L3)
E_Q4L3 <- round(E_Q4L3, digits = 3)
E_Q4L3


AEPFL3 <- cbind(E_P2L3, E_P3L3, E_P4L3)
AEQFL3 <- cbind(E_Q2L3, E_Q3L3, E_Q4L3)

AEAFL3 <- rbind(AEPFL3, AEQFL3)
colnames(AEAFL3) <- c("Population 2", "Population 3", "Population 4")
rownames(AEAFL3) <- c("P Frequency", "Q Frequency")
AEAFL3
```

### Expected and Observed Heterozygosity

Below I calculated expected and observed heterozygosity between each population at locus one. Observed data based on the averages from generated population and expected data based on originally set allele frequency values.

```{r}
#Expected at each population for Locus 11

EHZP1L3 <- c(Aa =  2 * p_1 * q_1)
EHZP1L3 

EHZP2L3 <- c(Aa =  2 * p_2 * q_2)
EHZP2L3 

EHZP3L3 <- c(Aa =  2 * p_3 * q_3)
EHZP3L3 

AEHZL3 <- rbind(EHZP1L3, EHZP2L3, EHZP3L3)

AEHZL3


#Observed
OHZP1L3 <- c(Aa =  fq_locus3[1,2])
OHZP1L3 

OHZP2L3 <- c(Aa =  fq_locus3[2,2])
OHZP2L3 

OHZP3L3 <- c(Aa =  fq_locus3[3,2])
OHZP3L3 

AOHZL3 <- rbind(OHZP1L3, OHZP2L3, OHZP3L3)

AOHZL3
```

### Genotype Counts

```{r}
#Grouped Graphs for Genotype Counts
par(mfrow = c(1,2))

ylimgc <- c(0, 40)
gc_locus3R <- round(gc_locus3, digits = 2)

SPGCL3 <- barplot(gc_locus3, col=colors()[c(36, 12, 55)], border = "white", font.axis = 1, beside = T, xlab="Genotype Count", font.lab=1, ylim = ylimgc)
colnames(SPGCL3) <- c("aa", "Aa", "AA")

```
